Snehalata Multispeciality Hospital, Nagpur
Department of Cardiology
Patient: Gopal Rao, 58 / Male
Admitted: 03/11/2026
Discharged: 08/11/2026

DIAGNOSIS: Non ST elevation myocardial infarction. Hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus.

HOSPITAL COURSE: Patient came with chest discomfort. Troponin positive. Managed with antiplatelets and heparin. Angiography showed double vessel disease, PTCA with DES to LAD. Stable at discharge.

HOME MEDICATIONS:
Tab. Telma AM 40 1-0-0
Tab. Ecosprin 75 1-0-0
Tab. Glycomet 500 1-0-1

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Tab. Ecosprin AV 75/10 1-0-0
2. Tab. Brilinta 90 1-0-1 x 12 months
3. Tab. Atorva 40 0-0-1
4. Tab. Glycomet 500 1-0-1 continue
5. Tab. Telma AM 40 1-0-0
6. Tab. Rosuvas 10 0-0-1 (replaced Atorva 20)
7. Syp. Digene 10 ml SOS

ADVICE: Cardiac rehabilitation after 2 weeks. No smoking.

FOLLOW UP: Cardiology OPD after 10 days i.e. 18/11/2026.

PENDING TESTS: Lipid profile, HbA1c after 1 month.

WARNING SIGNS: If chest pain or sweating returns, go to the emergency department immediately. If giddiness or blackouts, call your doctor.

MARIGOLD NURSING HOME, INDORE
GENERAL MEDICINE
Name: Farida Sheikh, 44 / F
IP No: MN-2026-5521
D.O.A.: 12/11/2026
D.O.D.: 16/11/2026

DIAGNOSIS: Community acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe.

HOSPITAL COURSE: Fever with cough for 5 days. Chest X-ray showed right lower lobe consolidation. Started on IV antibiotics, switched to oral. Afebrile for 48 hours before discharge.

MEDICATIONS ON DISCHARGE:
Tab. Augmentin 625 mg 1-1-1 x 5 days
Tab. Dolo 650 1-1-1 x 3 days
Tab. Levocet 5 0-0-1 x 7 days
Cap. Ventryl D 1-0-1 x 5 days
Syp. Ascoril LS 10 ml 1-0-1 x 5 days
Tab. Pan 40 1-0-0 before food x 5 days

DIET: Soft diet, plenty of fluids.

FOLLOW UP: Medicine OPD after 5 days with X-ray.

WARNING SIGNS: If breathlessness or fever above 100 returns, come to emergency immediately.

Sunrise Heritage Hospital, Hyderabad
Paediatrics
Patient: Aarav Menon, 6 years / M
Reg No: SHH-PED-2026-3312
Admitted: 20/11/2026
Discharged: 23/11/2026

DIAGNOSIS: Acute bronchiolitis.

HOSPITAL COURSE: Cough and fast breathing for 3 days. Hypoxia on admission, needed oxygen for 2 days. Fed well from day 2. Discharged in stable condition.

MEDICATIONS AT DISCHARGE:
Syp. Ascoril LS 2.5 ml 1-0-1 x 5 days
Syp. Crocin 250 5 ml SOS for fever
Neb. Levolin 1.25 mg via nebuliser TDS x 3 days
Neb. Budecort 0.5 mg via nebuliser BD x 5 days
Syp. Zincovit 5 ml 1-0-0 x 14 days

ADVICE: Steam inhalation. Small frequent feeds. Avoid smoke exposure.

FOLLOW UP: Paediatric OPD after 5 days.

WARNING SIGNS: If fast breathing returns, come to emergency immediately.

Greenfield Medical Centre, Lucknow
Obstetrics and Gynaecology
Name: Priyanka Trivedi, 29 / F
UR No: GMC/2026/9104
Admitted: 01/12/2026
Discharged: 04/12/2026

DIAGNOSIS: Full term normal delivery. Postpartum day 3. Anaemia (mild).

HOSPITAL COURSE: Spontaneous vaginal delivery, healthy baby girl. Third stage managed with oxytocin. Hemoglobin 10.2. Breastfeeding established. Discharged in stable condition.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Tab. Pan 40 1-0-0 before food x 14 days
Tab. Orofer 1-0-1 x 30 days
Cap. Calcirol 60 1 sachet weekly x 8 weeks
Tab. Shelcal HD 0-0-1 continue
Tab. Tranexa 500 1-0-1 x 5 days
Syp. Duphalac 15 ml HS x 7 days

ADVICE: Continue iron rich diet. Exclusive breastfeeding. Perineal hygiene.

FOLLOW UP: Obstetrics OPD after 14 days with baby for vaccination.

WARNING SIGNS: If heavy bleeding or fever, come to the emergency immediately.

Lotus Care Multispeciality Hospital, Pune
Orthopaedics
Patient: Harpreet Kaur, 67 / Female
MRN: LC-2026-91140
Admitted: 07/11/2026
Discharged: 13/11/2026

DIAGNOSIS: Osteoarthritis right knee. Post right total knee replacement (POD 6).

HOSPITAL COURSE: Elective total knee replacement done. Physiotherapy started from day 1. Wound healthy, staples removed. Knee flexion 100 degrees. DVT prophylaxis given during stay.

MEDICATIONS ON ADMISSION:
Tab. Telma 40 1-0-0
Tab. Shelcal HD 0-0-1

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Tab. Dolo 650 1-1-1 x 5 days
2. Tab. Combiflam SOS for pain
3. Tab. Ecosprin 75 1-0-0 continue
4. Tab. Rosuvas 10 0-0-1 continue
5. Tab. Pan 40 1-0-0 before food
6. Tab. Shelcal HD 0-0-1 continue
7. Inj. Enoxaparin 40 mg SC OD x 10 days
8. Tab. Dytor 10 1-0-0 x 7 days, then review

DIET: High protein diet.

ACTIVITY: Walker for 2 weeks. Knee exercises daily.

FOLLOW UP: Ortho OPD after 10 days with X-ray knee standing.

PENDING TESTS: CBC after 2 weeks.

WARNING SIGNS: If calf pain or swelling, or breathlessness, attend emergency immediately. If wound redness or discharge, call your doctor.

Anandam Hospital, Vijayawada
General Surgery
Patient: K. Ramesh Babu, 41 / M
IP No: AH-2026-77012
D.O.A.: 15th Nov
D.O.D.: 18th Nov 2026

DIAGNOSIS: Acute appendicitis. Post laparoscopic appendicectomy (POD 3).

HOSPITAL COURSE: Laparoscopic appendicectomy done on admission day. Histopathology sent. Tolerated orals from POD 1. Discharged in stable condition.

MEDICATIONS AT DISCHARGE:
Cap. Monocef O 200 1-0-1 x 5 days
Tab. Dolo 650 1-1-1 x 3 days
Tab. Combiflam SOS
Tab. Ondem 4 1-0-1 x 2 days
Syp. Cremaffin 15 ml HS x 5 days
Tab. Pan 40 1-0-0 before food x 5 days
Tab. Chymoral Forte 1-1-1 x 5 days

WOUND CARE: Keep wound clean and dry.

DIET: Clear fluids today, soft diet from tomorrow.

FOLLOW UP: Surgical OPD on 28/11/2026 with histopathology report. Stitch removal after 10 days.

WARNING SIGNS: Fever above 100, wound discharge or severe pain — attend surgical emergency immediately.

Marigold Hospital, Coimbatore
Neurology
Patient: Sundaram Iyer, 72 / M
IP No: MH-91-2026-5520
Admitted: 09/12/2026
Discharged: 15/12/2026

DIAGNOSIS: Acute ischaemic stroke left middle cerebral artery. Hypertension, atrial fibrillation.

HOSPITAL COURSE: Sudden right sided weakness and slurring of speech. Thrombolysed within 3 hours. Weakness improving at discharge. SWALLOW SAFE for tablets.

MEDICATIONS ON ADMISSION:
Tab. Telma 40 1-0-0
Tab. Metolar XR 25 1-0-0

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Tab. Ecosprin AV 75/10 1-0-0
2. Tab. Brilinta 90 1-0-1 x 21 days
3. Tab. Rosuvas 10 0-0-1
4. Tab. Telma 40 1-0-0 continue
5. Tab. Metolar XR 25 1-0-1 (increased from once daily)
6. Tab. Pan 40 1-0-0 before breakfast
7. Tab. Donecept 5 0-0-1 x 30 days
8. Syp. Duphalac 15 ml SOS

ADVICE: Physiotherapy daily. Swallow exercises. Blood pressure monitoring at home.

FOLLOW UP: Neurology OPD after 14 days with CT brain film. Physiotherapy review weekly.

PENDING TESTS: Lipid profile, HbA1c, echo after 1 month.

WARNING SIGNS: If weakness increases or new slurring, rush to emergency immediately (stroke can recur). If bleeding from gums or black stools, inform your doctor.

Snehalata Hospital, Nagpur
General Medicine
Name: Anita Deshmukh, 35 / F
IP: SN-2026-4412
Admitted: 27/11/2026
Discharged: 01/12/2026

DIAGNOSIS: Dengue fever with warning signs. Thrombocytopenia.

HOSPITAL COURSE: Fever with body ache and vomiting. Platelets dropped to 80,000. Given IV fluids. Platelet count rising at discharge (1.4 lakh). No bleeding manifestations.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Tab. Dolo 650 1-1-1 x 3 days
Tab. Pan 40 1-0-0 before food x 5 days
Tab. Ondem 4 SOS for vomiting
Syp. Zincovit 10 ml 1-0-0 x 15 days
Tab. Levocet 5 0-0-1 x 5 days for itching

ADVICE: Daily platelet monitoring for 3 days at local lab. Plenty of oral fluids. Avoid NSAIDs.

FOLLOW UP: Medicine OPD after 3 days with CBC report.

PENDING TESTS: CBC after 3 days.

WARNING SIGNS: If gum bleeding, black stools, severe abdominal pain or drowsiness, go to the emergency department immediately.

Greenfield Medical Centre, Lucknow
Pulmonology
Patient: Mohan Pillai, 54 / M
UR No: GMC/2026/8890
D.O.A.: 05/12/2026
D.O.D.: 09/12/2026

DIAGNOSIS: Acute exacerbation of COPD. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.

HOSPITAL COURSE: Increased cough with breathlessness. Neubilised with duolin and budecort. Steroids given, taper started. Sugars monitored. Improved to baseline.

HOME MEDICATIONS BEFORE ADMISSION:
Tab. Glycomet 500 1-0-1
Inj. Lantus 16 units HS
Tab. Duova 1-0-1

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Tab. Omnacortil 10 mg 1-0-0 x 5 days, then 5 mg 1-0-0 x 5 days, then stop
2. Cap. Duova 1-0-1 continue
3. Tab. Glycomet 500 1-0-1 continue
4. Inj. Lantus 16 units SC at bedtime
5. Syp. Ascoril LS 10 ml 1-0-1 x 7 days
6. Tab. Allegra 120 1-0-0 x 10 days
7. Tab. Pan 40 1-0-0 before food
8. Duolin HFA inhaler 2 puffs SOS

ADVICE: Inhaler technique rechecked. Avoid dust and smoke. Annual influenza vaccine.

FOLLOW UP: Pulmonology OPD after 10 days. Spirometry at visit.

PENDING TESTS: HbA1c at review.

WARNING SIGNS: If speech difficulty with breathlessness or lips turning blue, rush to the emergency immediately.

Anandam Hospital, Vijayawada
Endocrinology
Patient: Sunita Verma, 48 / F
IP No: AH-2026-70021
Admitted: 18/11/2026
Discharged: 21/11/2026

DIAGNOSIS: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, uncontrolled. Diabetic ketoacidosis (recovered).

HOSPITAL COURSE: Vomiting and high sugars (RBS 420). Corrected with IV fluids and insulin infusion. Shifted to basal bolus. Ketones cleared. Hypoglycaemia education given.

MEDICATIONS ON DISCHARGE:
Inj. Basalog 18 units SC at bedtime
Inj. Human Actrapid 8 units SC before breakfast and 6 units before dinner
Tab. Glycomet 500 1-0-1
Tab. Pan 40 1-0-0 before food
Tab. Thyronorm 50 1-0-0 before breakfast
Tab. Shelcal HD 0-0-1

ADVICE: Home glucose monitoring twice daily. Carry glucose meter and diary to every visit. If sugar below 70, take 15 g sugar immediately.

DIET: 1600 kcal diabetic diet. Walk 30 minutes daily.

FOLLOW UP: Diabetes OPD on 28/11/2026 with sugar diary.

PENDING TESTS: HbA1c, urine microalbumin, fundus examination.

WARNING SIGNS: If vomiting returns with rapid breathing, go to hospital immediately. If wound on foot does not heal, inform your doctor.

Sunrise Heritage Hospital, Hyderabad
Nephrology
Patient: Abdul Rahman, 61 / M
Reg No: SHH-NEP-2026-0091
Admitted: 22/11/2026
Discharged: 28/11/2026

DIAGNOSIS: Chronic kidney disease stage 4. Acute on chronic kidney injury (recovering). Hypertension.

HOSPITAL COURSE: Urea 140, creatinine 5.8 at admission. Fluids and diuretics. Creatinine 3.9 at discharge. Urine output adequate. Nephrology follow up planned.

HOME MEDICATIONS:
Tab. Telma 40 1-0-0
Tab. Dytor 10 1-0-0
Tab. Shelcal HD 0-0-1

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Tab. Telma 40 1-0-0 continue
2. Tab. Dytor 10 1-0-1 (increased)
3. Tab. Pan 40 1-0-0 before food
4. Tab. Ondem 4 1-0-1 x 5 days
5. Tab. Ecosprin 75 1-0-0 hold till nephrology review
6. Tab. Shelcal HD 0-0-1 continue
7. Syp. Duphalac 15 ml HS continue

DIET: Low potassium, low salt diet. Fluid restriction 1 litre per day.

FOLLOW UP: Nephrology OPD after 7 days with creatinine report. Dialysis counselling at visit if needed.

PENDING TESTS: Serum creatinine, electrolytes, ultrasound KUB after 1 week.

WARNING SIGNS: If decreased urine output, breathlessness at night or swelling increases, come to emergency immediately.

Lotus Care Hospital, Pune
Oncology Day Care
Patient: Vasanti Patil, 52 / F
MRN: LC-2026-4471
Admitted: 30/11/2026
Discharged: 30/11/2026

DIAGNOSIS: Carcinoma right breast, post chemotherapy cycle 3. Neutropenia (recovered).

HOSPITAL COURSE: Day care admission for chemotherapy. Tolerated well with antiemetics. Discharged same evening with oral medications.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Tab. Ondem 8 1-0-1 x 3 days
Tab. Dexa 4 1-0-1 x 3 days
Tab. Pan 40 1-0-0 before food x 5 days
Tab. Cloheal Plus 1-0-0 x 7 days
Cap. Ventryl D 1-0-1 x 5 days
Tab. Zolfresh 5 0-0-1 x 5 days
Syp. Duphalac 15 ml SOS

ADVICE: Report fever above 100 immediately — it is an emergency during chemotherapy.

FOLLOW UP: Medical oncology OPD after 14 days for cycle 4. CBC after 7 days.

WARNING SIGNS: Fever above 100 F — attend emergency immediately. Severe vomiting or mouth ulcers — call your doctor.
